A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe DMRetriever and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Existing content can be matched reliably, including renumbered tables and the relocated Figure 8.

before.justification: v1 reports original DisastIR-Test retrieval results, model ablations, contamination analysis, and measurements of DisastIR-DevLite efficiency and effectiveness.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for three knowledge-distilled DMRetriever variants in Appendix L and Table 8.

M1.justification: Appendix M adds a knowledge-distillation procedure producing 33M, 109M, and 335M DMRetriever-KD variants from already fine-tuned models. It introduces intent-specific teacher scores as soft labels and combines contrastive and KL-divergence losses. This adds a substantive training component beyond v1's retained three-stage pipeline.

E1.justification: The represented domains, English-language coverage, six retrieval intents, and DisastIR evaluation coverage remain unchanged. MTT-0.95-KD extends existing MTT-0.95 with teacher scores; it does not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 8 adds evaluated comparisons against e5-small-v2, e5-base-v2, e5-large-v2, and granite-embedding-125m. v1 explicitly excluded these distilled baselines in Section 4.2 and Appendix G. Including this previously excluded comparator class substantially broadens the evidence for compact models, while the original 29-baseline comparison remains intact.

E3.justification: The added KD experiment starts from fine-tuned 33M, 109M, and 335M models and trains with teacher-labeled MTT-0.95-KD. This introduces an additional experimental condition. The existing data splits, retrieval metric, original difficulty schedules, and evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: The data-component, filtering, progressive-training, attention, and instruction ablations are unchanged, as are contamination and DevLite analyses. The new KD table reports benchmark comparisons rather than a controlled KD ablation. Figure 8 is relocated without changing its analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Table 2's one-tailed Wilcoxon signed-rank test with p < 0.05. v2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or additional statistical procedures for the KD results.

E6.justification: Table 8 adds a substantive result set covering three KD variants and four distilled baselines across all six intents. The KD variants report averages of 63.84, 65.68, and 66.14. These are additional results under different training conditions; the original variants' averages of 58.61, 59.97, and 62.85, and the other existing results, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix M introduces the mathematical definition L_KD = L_CL + lambda L_KL for the new distillation objective. Existing equations and algorithms remain unchanged, and no new theorem, proof, or formal guarantee is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same domain-specialization, six-intent performance, and parameter-efficiency claims. The introduction emphasizes progressive instruction fine-tuning, which v1 already explicitly proposed; this is a reframing of an existing contribution rather than a new core scientific claim.

C2.justification: Appendix L extends the practical interpretation to KD models, arguing that their performance relative to much larger models makes them suitable for resource-limited, low-latency disaster-management applications. The existing mechanism explanations and English-language and text-only limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix M newly documents teacher selection by search intent, construction of soft-labeled MTT-0.95-KD, initialization from fine-tuned models, and a distillation weight of lambda = 1. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, and resource-access information remain unchanged; KD-specific optimization settings are not separately detailed.

R1.justification: Appendix L positions DMRetriever-KD as a fair counterpart to distilled models such as E5, extending v1's discussion that only justified excluding them. The cited-work set and related-work section remain unchanged; corrected author formatting for existing references is bibliographic editing.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized terminology and contribution-description edits, corrects several reference author lists, and appends Sections L and M. The main narrative and existing section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the KD comparison as Table 8, renumbers subsequent tables, and moves the unchanged Figure 8 from page 17 to page 18. Figure 2's framework label and caption are revised. The remaining plots and overall document layout are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendices L–M and Table 8 reduce v1's comparison gap by evaluating compact KD variants against previously excluded E5 and Granite baselines and explaining the new objective. This strengthens the comparative evidence. The gain remains limited: KD-specific optimization details are incomplete, and no matched control isolates distillation from additional training on MTT-0.95. The original results and analyses remain intact.
